item.title: How to brew better pour-over at home
item.description: A simple, repeatable pour-over recipe: the ratio, grind, water temperature and pour timing that turn good beans into a great cup, with no special gear.

item.title: Light, medium or dark roast: what actually changes
item.description: What really changes between light, medium and dark roasts: flavor, acidity, body and caffeine, and how to choose the right roast for the way you brew.

item.title: How we choose the farms we buy from
item.description: How our buyer picks farms and lots: the cupping scores, relationships and traceability that decide which coffees make it into a Tidewell bag.

item.title: Why freshness matters: the case for roast dates
item.description: Why a roast date beats a best-before date, how long coffee stays at its best, and how to store beans so you get the most from every bag.

item.title: Grind size, explained
item.description: Grind size is the fastest way to fix a cup that tastes sour or bitter. Learn what each grind does and the right setting for every brewer.
